channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Eleições 2026 AO VIVO: Acompanhe a votação para Presidente no 1º turno
item.description: The 2026 first-round presidential election in Brazil is underway, also deciding governors, senators, and federal deputies. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead the polls, followed by Augusto Cury, Renan Santos, and Caiado.

item.title: Moro vota em Curitiba, celebra decisão do TSE sobre Deltan e defende campanha limpa
item.description: Sérgio Moro, a PL candidate for Governor of Paraná, voted this Sunday in Curitiba and celebrated the TSE ruling that secured Deltan Dallagnol's eligibility. The former judge advocated for a clean campaign and reaffirmed his anti-corruption stance following the favorable verdict.

item.title: Augusto Cury (Avante) vota em Colina, interior de São Paulo
item.description: Presidential candidate Augusto Cury (Avante) cast his vote in Colina, an inland city in São Paulo state, around 11 a.m. this Sunday, the 4th. He is running for the Planalto Palace on a ticket with Júlio Delgado, also from Avante.

item.title: Tarcísio: 'tenho visto migração de outros candidatos para Flávio Bolsonaro, estou otimista'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, running for reelection, stated that he sees a migration of voters from other right-wing candidates in support of Flávio Bolsonaro and expressed optimism about the electoral scenario. He emphasized the current movement of consolidating the conservative base for the 2026 elections.

item.title: TSE: 55 auditores do TCU acompanham teste de integridade no Brasil; não há intercorrências
item.description: The TSE reported that 421 voting machines were replaced and 55 TCU auditors are monitoring the integrity test without incidents.

item.title: Brasileiros votam na Itália: eleitorado cresce em 2026, mas índice de abstenção é alto
item.description: Brazilians in Italy prepare for 2026 voting with increased participation, but face high abstention rates. In Rome, Piazza Navona divides between political groups, reflecting polarization of the Brazilian electorate abroad. The atmosphere mixes celebration with tension between different ideological orientations.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP, diz que eleição foi vazia e chama Flávio Bolsonaro de ‘desqualificado, covarde e burro’
item.description: Renan Santos, federal congressman elected from São Paulo, publicly criticized the 2026 election as 'meaningless' and launched a scathing personal attack on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him 'disqualified, cowardly, and stupid.' His remarks sparked mixed reactions in the political arena, with condemnations over disrespect and defenses citing freedom of speech.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP e diz que eleição é ‘a mais bizarra de todas’
item.description: Candidate Renan Santos (Missão) voted in São Paulo and harshly criticized the election, calling it 'the strangest ever', arguing that no proposals were discussed and major political forces are embroiled in corruption scandals.

item.title: Brasileiro tem o direito de sonhar, diz Cury ao votar
item.description: Augusto Cury, Avante's presidential candidate, voted in Colina (SP) and emphasized the vote as a transformative tool, stating: 'Neither steak nor rifle, Augusto Cury to change Brazil'. A recent poll shows Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied with 46% of voting intentions for a potential second round, while Cury has 3% in the first round.

item.title: Elecciones en Brasil 2026, en vivo | Lula y Bolsonaro votan en la primera vuelta por la presidencia
item.description: Brazil holds one of its most competitive presidential elections, with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeking reelection and Flávio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, running on the right. Lula expressed confidence in victory, while Bolsonaro claimed the country needs change. This first round will determine who advances to a potential runoff.

item.title: Haddad diz que fez “grande campanha” e sai “com espírito leve”
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) stated after voting in the 2026 municipal elections that he ran a 'great campaign' and leaves with a light spirit, highlighting the climate of dialogue and openness among São Paulo voters. He thanked voters and noted the atmosphere is better than in 2022.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em 'voto de revolta'; Lula aposta em 'dia glorioso'; veja como foi a manhã dos candidatos
item.description: Presidential candidates Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) cast their ballots Sunday morning, highlighting the electoral uncertainty shown in recent polls. Both remain statistically tied in the latest surveys ahead of the 2026 first-round vote.

item.title: Presidente do STF, Edson Fachin vota no 1º turno das Eleições 2026
item.description: The President of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), Minister Edson Fachin, voted in the first round of the 2026 elections in Brasília, emphasizing the importance of voting as an expression of popular sovereignty and highlighting the role of the Electoral Justice in ensuring a transparent election.

item.title: Eleições no RJ: principais candidatos ao governo do estado já votaram
item.description: Voters in Rio de Janeiro cast their ballots on Sunday (4) in municipal and state elections, choosing candidates for federal deputy, state deputy, two Senate seats, governor, and president. Voting takes place from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Brasília time, and a voter ID card is not required—only an official photo ID.

item.title: Fachin vota em Brasília
item.description: The President of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and National Justice Council (CNJ), Luiz Edson Fachin, voted in Brasília on Sunday. He attended the Centro de Ensino Fundamental 214 Sul in the Asa Sul district, waited in line and spoke with voters. Fachin stated he will address the press after completing his vote, emphasizing the importance of conscious voting.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas vota e prega humildade na espera pelo resultado
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas voted in the first round of the São Paulo elections and called for humility while awaiting the count, expressing optimism and highlighting the support received during the campaign.

item.title: Meia da seleção australiana, Irvine demonstra apoio a Lula nas redes
item.description: Australian national team player Jackson Irvine expressed support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) on social media by featuring the candidate's number 13 in posts on election Sunday. He also paid tribute to Sócrates, former Corinthians player associated with the Democracia Corintiana movement. Irvine, currently playing for Cerezo Osaka, is a key figure in Australia's national squad.

item.title: Quantas urnas precisaram ser trocadas pelo TSE por falhas técnicas na manhã do primeiro turno
item.description: The TSE reported that 421 electronic voting machines were replaced by 10 AM on election day due to technical failures, representing 0.07% of all equipment in use. São Paulo leads replacement occurrences with 86 cases, followed by Paraná with 60. The Electoral Justice maintains contingency machines and technical teams monitoring equipment security with no irregularities recorded.

item.title: Haddad vota acompanhado de Alckmin, Marina e Tebet: ‘saindo com espírito leve’
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) voted accompanied by Alckmin, Marina, Tebet, and Márcio França, highlighting the dialogue atmosphere of the campaign. He thanked voters and expressed satisfaction, emphasizing the light spirit of the campaign. Before voting, he had breakfast with Lula, whom he described as being in good spirits.

item.title: Eleições 2026: acompanhe a apuração em todo o Brasil pelo g1
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections, held on October 4, elected governors, senators, federal and state deputies, and the president. Results were streamed live by G1 using TSE data, featuring interactive maps and zone-level vote tracking. Voters could access detailed results, including votes per municipality and polling booth, enhancing electoral transparency.

item.title: Zema descumpre regra e usa celular na cabine de votação
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo presidential candidate, was caught entering the voting booth in Araxá (MG) with two cell phones, violating electoral rules. Press footage captured the moment, and the case was referred to the TRE-MG, where officials deemed the behavior irregular and potentially punishable. Zema denied recording or photographing his vote, claiming he was not warned by poll workers about the restriction.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP e dispara contra Flávio: “Covarde e burro”
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential candidate from the Missão party, voted in São Paulo's southern zone and launched attacks against Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him 'cowardly and stupid' and questioning his performance and voter support.

item.title: Apuração fora do Brasil: acompanhe as votações para presidente nas urnas do exterior
item.description: Brazilians abroad have already voted in the 2026 presidential election, with Lula leading in countries like New Zealand, South Korea, and Australia. Flávio Bolsonaro won in the Philippines and Thailand, while long lines formed in Portugal for voting. The vote count continues live as time zones allow results to be released.

item.title: Raquel Lyra vota em Caruaru (PE)
item.description: Governor and re-election candidate Raquel Lyra (PSD) voted at the Diocesan College of Caruaru, in Pernambuco, on Sunday (4th), during the state race against former mayor João Campos (PSB). According to the latest Quaest poll, Lyra leads with 52% of valid votes, compared to 47% for Campos, in a survey registered with the TSE and commissioned by Globo.

item.title: Deltan vai a Fux contra pedido analisado por Dino sobre votos no Paraná
item.description: Candidate for Senate from Paraná, Deltan Dallagnol (Novo), filed a lawsuit with Minister Luiz Fux to prevent Minister Flávio Dino from reviewing a petition that could disallow votes received by him. The case involves a dispute over Deltan's candidacy and reached the STF following a TSE ruling. His defense argues that analyzing the petition violates a prior suspension granted by Fux.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes viaja de Brasília a Cuiabá para votar nas eleições
item.description: STF Minister Gilmar Mendes voted in the 2026 elections in Diamantino (MT), his hometown, carrying only his ID and candidate notes. The elections include positions like president, governor, senator, federal and state deputies, with Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as main candidates.

item.title: Governador Tarcísio de Freitas afirma estar otimista com votação, mas evita dizer que eleição está ganha
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) cast his ballot Sunday morning at Colégio Miguel de Cervantes in São Paulo and expressed optimism about the vote, while avoiding claims that the election is already decided. His stance reflects strategic caution ahead of the election.

item.title: Imprensa internacional relaciona rumo da América Latina à eleição no Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian presidential election on October 4th is highlighted as a crucial point for Latin America's future, with the race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro capturing international press attention. The campaign is marked by corruption scandals involving both sides and electoral polarization, with a possible runoff on October 25th.

item.title: Sobrinho de Dilma e deputado do PT batem boca com eleitores em BH
item.description: Pedro Rousseff and Rogério Correia clashed with voters in Belo Horizonte during Dilma's voting, amid shouts and scuffles. Pedro said the environment was dangerous and that there was a risk to his aunt's safety, emphasizing the importance of the moment to contain Bolsonarism. The two labeled protesters as fascists and stressed the need for security.

item.title: 'A expectativa é a melhor possível', diz Tarcísio ao votar em São Paulo
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) spoke while voting in São Paulo, expressing his highest possible expectations regarding the election outcome for himself, his party, and allies. He conveyed strategic optimism without addressing specific issues such as economy, security, or healthcare.

item.title: Local de votação 2026: como consultar sua zona, seção e saber onde votar
item.description: Voters can check their polling place, including electoral zone and section, online or by phone for the 2026 elections. The first round takes place on the 4th, from 8am to 5pm, nationwide.

item.title: Como justificar o voto nas Eleições 2026? Veja prazo e passo a passo
item.description: Electors who cannot vote in the 2026 elections can justify their absence via e-Title, online, or in person. The procedure varies depending on whether the justification is made on election day or after the vote. The justification must be submitted within the deadlines set by the TSE.

item.title: Brasileiros votam em eleições acompanhadas de perto por Donald Trump
item.description: Brazilians vote between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, deciding if the country will follow Trump's conservative wave.

item.title: Flávio tem 50,2% e Lula, 47,4% em 2º turno em MG, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel/ Estadão poll in Minas Gerais shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 50.2% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) at 47.4% in a hypothetical runoff, within the 2-point margin of error, indicating a statistical tie. The survey also reveals that 53% of Minas Gerais voters disapprove of Lula's administration.

item.title: Candidatos a deputado federal por São Paulo (SP): confira nome e números
item.description: The federal deputy election in São Paulo takes place on October 4, 2026, with 70 seats contested and over 34 million voters. Voters must enter the candidate's four-digit number and confirm, being able to check the photo, name, party, and status at the TSE.

item.title: Eleições 2026: votação é encerrada no Japão, onde filas foram registradas
item.description: Voting in the 2026 elections for Brazilians in Japan concluded with reported long lines and delays due to confusing instructions about required documents. Witnesses noted that volunteers struggled to guide voters, particularly the elderly, causing extended wait times. A total of 918,911 overseas voters are eligible, with 1,407 electronic voting machines across 134 countries.

item.title: Candidatos a deputado estadual pelo Rio de Janeiro (RJ): confira nome e números
item.description: The 2026 elections in Rio de Janeiro will feature 70 seats in the State Legislative Assembly (Alerj), with candidates identified by five-digit numbers. Voters must verify the photo, name, number, and party before confirming their vote and can check candidate lists and their status at the TSE. The Electoral Justice recommends writing down candidate numbers, as mobile phones are not allowed inside voting booths.

item.title: 80% das doações recebidas por presidenciáveis são repasses de PT e PL feitos para Lula e Flávio
item.description: Presidential candidates received R$ 164 million in donations, with 80% coming from direct transfers by the PT to Lula and the PL to Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula leads with R$ 77.3 million, while Flávio raised R$ 61.9 million. Flávio's campaign relies on 89% of its funding from the PL, and 97% of Lula's donations came from his party.

item.title: Eleições 2026 têm politização do STF, força do centrão, golpe baixo e feridas abertas; veja análises
item.description: The 2026 elections are marked by the strong presence of the STF and TSE, deepening polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Analyses highlight the Centrão's power in the Legislature and institutional tensions that may affect the election outcome.

item.title: Posso ir votar com camisa, bóton ou boné do meu candidato?
item.description: Voters are allowed to wear shirts, caps, or badges of their candidates on election day, as the TSE permits silent expression. However, any form of pressure, coercion, or active campaigning—such as distributing flyers, soliciting votes, or organizing group demonstrations—is prohibited near polling stations. Violations may result in heavy fines, criminal charges, and imprisonment of six months to one year.

item.title: Pesquisas de véspera reforçam aposta de Flávio Bolsonaro no voto útil
item.description: Pre-election polls show Flávio Bolsonaro statistically tied with Lula, reinforcing the strategy to mobilize right-wing and center-right voters for the first round. Flávio's campaign bets on support from voters of Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos, while Lula remains confident in advancing to the second round with a numerical lead.

item.title: Eleições 2026: transporte público será gratuito no DF neste domingo (4/10)
item.description: Public transportation in the Federal District will be free on Sunday (October 4th) for the first round of the 2026 General Elections, according to TSE Resolution No. 23,751/2026. The measure aims to ensure the free exercise of citizenship and also applies to a potential second round scheduled for October 25th.

item.title: Longas filas logo na abertura das urnas em Portugal
item.description: Thousands of Brazilians queued for hours at polling stations in Portugal for the 2026 vote, with slower lines in Lisbon and faster processing in Porto. The organization faced criticism over poor signage, but voting proceeded without major incidents.

item.title: Eleições 2026: entenda como funciona o voto de brasileiros no exterior
item.description: The 2026 elections abroad began before the first round in Brazil, with 918,876 Brazilians eligible to vote in 134 countries. Voting is organized by the Overseas Electoral Zone (ZZ) together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and voters only choose the president and vice-president. The largest electorate is in the United States, followed by Portugal and Japan.

item.title: Da desconfiança à reta final: a caminhada de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reaches the first round with 40% of voting intentions, behind Lula (45%), after overcoming internal crises, friendly fire, and doubts about campaign continuity. Initially marked by uncertainties and difficult alliances, his candidacy consolidated with Jair Bolsonaro's support and the PL as its base. The campaign was also impacted by fake news, investigations, and movements from allies like Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: Eleições sob chuva: confira a previsão do tempo no Brasil neste domingo
item.description: The first round of elections takes place under rain across much of Brazil, with storm risks in the South and heavy rains in the Southeast and Center-West, according to the National Institute of Meteorology.

item.title: Flávio se concentrou em Lula, STF e segurança pública na campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro focused his electoral campaign on criticizing Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the Supreme Federal Court, emphasizing public security and corruption. Between August 16 and October 3, he posted 41 critical messages about Lula and 19 attacks on Supreme Court ministers, particularly Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino. His strategy included controversial proposals, such as declaring criminal organizations as terrorist groups and chemical castration for rapists.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Brasileiros votam no EUA em meio à tensão com ICE
item.description: Over 265,000 Brazilian voters in the US face fear of voting in the 2026 elections due to intensified ICE operations. The Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Embassy are setting up 344 polling stations to reduce risks, but immigration enforcement concerns may lower turnout. Overseas voting is limited to president and vice-president.

item.title: Mais de 158 milhões de brasileiros vão às urnas para decidir futuro do país
item.description: Over 158.7 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in general elections that will decide the president, governors, senators, and legislators. Lula (PT) faces Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), while former president Jair Bolsonaro is ineligible and under house arrest after being convicted of attempted coup.

item.title: Eleições 2026: saiba onde votam os candidatos à Presidência
item.description: The first round of the 2026 presidential elections takes place this Sunday (October 4th), with 12 candidates voting across various locations in Brazil. Most candidates have their electoral residence in the Southeast region, including figures such as Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema. Voting times and addresses vary according to each candidate's home region.
